newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums erratic on French strike.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums erratic on French strike.

text.p: NWE heating oil cargo premiums seesawed uncertainly on Wednesday with traders apparently divided over the extent to which the French oil workers' strike is likely to support the NWE physical market.
Now in its seventh day, a strike of Elf workers has closed output from from the group's three refineries.
"Everyone is waiting for Elf to buy on the spot market but up to now they have been very relaxed," one French trader said. "They try to optimise (output) with other refineries instead."
Heating oil refinery grade cargoes were offered between Dec IPE +$3-7, eliciting bids at around +$2/2.50 in inactive trade. Low sulphur diesel was steady at around Dec IPE +$17/18.
Estimates of the amount of gas oil removed from the market by the strike varied between 120,000-400,000 tonnes.
Some traders said the effect of the strike was balanced by relatively mild weather in Germany and demand was being deflated by price strength driven by New York gasoline and crude.
Dec IPE futures gained $1.25 to $224.00 a tonne, after bouncing off lows in sympathy with firmer Brent crude futures.
Barge premiums were stable with heating oil at Dec IPE +$1.25/1.75 and low sulphur diesel at +$12/13.50 fob ARA.
